Pursuant to the remand of the matter by the APTEL in Appeal No. 137/2019, the Petitioner filed IA No. 3/2025 on 11.12.2024. The Respondent APDCL filed its reply thereto on 24.3.2025, and the Petitioner filed its rejoinder on 11.4.2025. However, as far as the contractual delays are concerned, it is always the responsibility of the work-assigning agency, in this case, the Petitioner, to maintain proper coordination and check up on the award and execution of the contract, and it is the responsibility of the Petitioner to ensure that the work is completed within the scheduled date. The labour strike is the Petitioner's failure, caused by improper management of the contract. Moreover, as per contract procedure, there is a declared completion date with terms and conditions, and any violation of the contract terms and conditions would entail the contractor being subject to imposition of penalty or recovery of LD. In view of the above, the delay in the completion of work due to labour strike cannot be said to be beyond the control of the Petitioner.
